messages:
eliza_support: FYI customer reported that their month-end invoice is ~18% higher than the dashboard total. Customer: Acme Analytics. They attached a screenshot of the invoice and the dashboard summary.

raj_finance: Can you paste the invoice line items and the dashboard export? I can start by comparing totals + plan tier.

eliza_support: Attached CSV excerpt in thread (pasted below). Key oddity: invoice has two 'Dedicated compute - burst' lines on 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-01 that sum to a large spike. Dashboard shows only one aggregated burst line on 2026-03-01.

linh_cs: Quick note from the customer: they upgraded plan mid-cycle (standard -> pro) on 2026-02-15. They expect prorated charges, not duplicated burst charges.

alex_sre: tagging billing-bot to see if any backfill jobs wrote duplicate usage rows at month boundary. @billing-bot any recent backfills?

billing-bot: Runbook check: nightly backfill completed 2026-03-02 03:12 UTC. No errors reported. A small job retried and created 2 identical ingest batches for partition p2026-02-28-00.

raj_finance: That sounds like a likely cause — duplicate ingestion at the partition level would double-charge on invoice but dashboard may dedupe by ingestion id. Need repro SQL to confirm.

eliza_support: I ran a quick query over the ledger for Acme that shows two rows with identical usage_id but different created_at. Pasting simplified output:```\n| usage_id           | account_id | tokens | source    | created_at          |\n| ------------------ | ---------- | ------ | --------- | ------------------- |\n| u_xxx_dup_001      | acct_acme  | 125000 | bursting  | 2026-03-02T03:08Z   |\n| u_xxx_dup_001      | acct_acme  | 125000 | bursting  | 2026-03-02T03:12Z   |\n```

linh_cs: Dashboard exporter groups by usage_id and keeps the earliest row; invoice generation uses raw ledger rows, so duplicates would show up on invoice.

alex_sre: OK repro path found. Root cause: backfill retried after a partial success and didn't mark the partial batch as idempotent. The ingestion job inserts rather than upserts. I'll open a PR to make the backfill idempotent and add dedupe by (usage_id, partition).

raj_finance: Short-term mitigation: We can run a cleanup that collapses duplicates for affected accounts before re-issuing credits. Two options: issue a manual credit for the duplicate amount, or correct the ledger and re-run invoice generation for Acme. Which is lower risk?

eliza_support: Customer wants a corrected invoice rather than a credit. They said their accounting team requires a single corrected invoice.

raj_finance: Understood. We should do ledger correction + regenerated invoice. Alex, can SRE schedule a ledger correction window and provide an audit log of changes? I'll need exact delta and justification for finance records.

alex_sre: I'll prepare a safe SQL patch to remove exact duplicate rows where (usage_id, account_id, tokens, source) are identical and created_at is a retry timestamp > earliest for that usage_id. Will run in a staging ledger first and share diff. ETA 4 hours.

linh_cs: I'll keep Acme updated and set expectation: corrected invoice within 48 hours, and we'll provide credit note + explanation.

billing-bot: Action items created: BK-4521 (ledger-dedupe-Acme), BK-4522 (backfill-idempotency-fix). Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BK-4521 | BK-4522

eliza_support: Thanks everyone. I'll attach the customer's CSV and escalate to priority-high. Will update thread when SRE posts the staging diff. :thumbsup:
